title: Why the Casino Always Wins
objective: After this level you can explain the house edge, using the extra green pockets on an American roulette wheel.
summary: An American roulette wheel has 38 pockets but pays single numbers 35 to 1, as if it had 36. The gap is a house edge of about 5.26% (2.7% on a single-zero wheel).

cards.headline: An American roulette wheel has 38 pockets. It pays as if it had 36.
cards.body: That small gap is the whole business. Here's how two green pockets turn a game of luck into a steady income for the casino.

cards.headline: Two green pockets
cards.body: The wheel has 38 pockets: 1 to 36 in red and black, plus a green 0 and 00. Bet $1 on one number and a win pays 35 to 1: you collect $35 and keep your dollar. But with 1 winning pocket and 37 losing ones, the true odds are 37 to 1 against. A 35 to 1 payout would be fair only on a wheel of 36 pockets.

cards.headline: Where the casino's cut comes from
cards.body: Picture betting $1 on one number for 38 spins, with your number hitting once, just as the average says. You staked $38 and get back $36: $35 in winnings plus your dollar. You're $2 down. That's 2 parts in 38, or about 5.26%: the house edge. In Level 32's terms, the bet's expected value is minus 5.26 cents per dollar.

cards.fact: Almost every bet on the American wheel carries the same edge: about 5.26%.
cards.context: Red or black, odd or even, a single number: the payouts are set as if the green pockets weren't there. A European wheel has just one green 0, which cuts the edge to about 2.7%. Any one player can get lucky tonight. But expected value is the long-run average, so across many bets the casino keeps close to 5.26 cents of every dollar.

cards.headline: The house edge: found
learned: House edge about 5.26% (2.7% with one zero)
Over many bets, the casino keeps its edge

questions.prompt: How do the green 0 and 00 give the casino its edge?

options.label: The ball lands in the green pockets more often
options.rationale: Each pocket is one of 38; the edge comes from the payouts.

options.label: Payouts are set as if the wheel had only 36 pockets
The casino takes a fee from every win
options.rationale: No fee is needed; the payout itself is short.

options.label: Players must also bet on green each spin
options.rationale: No such rule; the edge is built into the payouts.

questions.prompt: A $1 bet on one number wins $35 one time in 38 and loses $1 otherwise. Using Level 32's method, what is its expected value?

options.label: About plus 92 cents
options.rationale: That counts the $35 win but forgets the 37 losing pockets.

options.label: Zero: it is a fair game
options.rationale: The payout is short of the true odds, so it is not fair.

options.label: Minus $1
options.rationale: That's the loss on a single losing spin, not the average.

questions.explanation: $35 × 1/38 minus $1 × 37/38 is minus 2/38, about minus 5.26 cents per dollar.
